$comment: DESIGN PROPOSAL ONLY -- not wired into openrpc/launch.openrpc.json. Shape matches that file's components.schemas style exactly, and composes with design/site-config-v2.openrpc-fragment.json's SiteLaunchSpecWorker/SiteLaunchSpecDeployment additions (see design/plugin-basic-auth.md and design/plugin-telemetry-store.md for the full write-ups). This is the shared piece: how a SiteLaunch document opts a site into the basic-auth and telemetry-store plugins, and how SiteReveal grows a telemetryStorage section.

schemas.$comment_opt_in_shape: Two independent, additive opt-ins, matching the granularity of the two plugins: 'auth' inherently carries config (username/password) so its own presence on spec IS the opt-in -- no separate enum entry needed. 'telemetry-store' needs no per-site config (nothing to fill in beyond on/off), so it's a plain enum member of a general-purpose spec.plugins toggle array, left open for future config-free plugins.

username.description: HTTP Basic Auth username for this site's protected Gateway routes.

password.description: Plaintext password, submitted once over the same transport as the seed-phrase flow (this launcher assumes TLS terminates upstream, e.g. Railway's edge -- see src/session.js's x-forwarded-proto handling). The launcher hashes this immediately on receipt (scrypt, random per-site salt) and discards the plaintext: it is never stored in the SiteRecord, never included in sites.reveal or the downloadable spec.yaml, and never passed to the child process -- only the salt+hash are, via env vars. See design/plugin-basic-auth.md 'Password handling' for the full reasoning and design/plugins/basic-auth/lib/guard.js for the verifying side.

SiteLaunchSpecAuth.description: New, optional. Omitting this object entirely means the site has no basic-auth protection (today's behavior, unchanged) -- its presence is itself the opt-in, there is no separate 'enable basic-auth' flag to also set. Sibling of 'worker'/'deployment' from design/site-config-v2.openrpc-fragment.json inside SiteLaunch.spec.

PluginName.description: Closed set of config-free plugins a site can opt into via spec.plugins. Only one member today (telemetry-store); basic-auth is deliberately NOT in this enum because it always needs config and is opted into via spec.auth's presence instead (see SiteLaunchSpecAuth). A future config-free plugin would be added here without touching spec.auth's shape.

SiteLaunchSpecPlugins.description: New, optional. Omit (or []) for today's behavior: no extra plugins, unchanged from what ships now. Listing 'telemetry-store' boots the site with design/plugins/telemetry-store registered via extraPluginDirs, appending every polled telemetry read to an on-disk CSV under this site's .mdk-data root (see design/plugin-telemetry-store.md).

SiteLaunch_v2_plus_plugins_spec_EXAMPLE.$comment: Illustrative only -- this is what components.schemas.SiteLaunch.properties.spec becomes once design/site-config-v2.openrpc-fragment.json's worker/deployment additions AND this fragment's auth/plugins additions are all merged in. Required stays ['template','persistence']: every new field here is additive and optional, matching the backward-compatibility rule design/site-config-v2.md section 4 already establishes for worker/deployment.

worker.$comment: From design/site-config-v2.openrpc-fragment.json's components.schemas.SiteLaunchSpecWorker -- shown here only to illustrate composition, not a resolvable cross-file $ref.

schemas.$comment_SiteReveal: Additive to the EXISTING components.schemas.SiteReveal in openrpc/launch.openrpc.json (read there first -- required: ['siteId','slot','state','requestCurl','storage','telemetry'], additionalProperties: false): one new optional sibling property of 'storage'/'telemetry', populated only when 'telemetry-store' is in spec.plugins. Also tightens 'storage.path' /'requestCurl' handling: see the redaction note below.

TelemetryStorageMechanism.description: Which on-disk mechanism telemetry-store used. Only 'csv' today (design/plugin-telemetry-store.md's choice) -- kept as an enum, not a boolean, so a future 'sqlite' implementation is additive, not a breaking rename.

bytesPerHour.description: sizeBytes / hours elapsed between the first and most recent recorded sample. null until at least two distinct sample timestamps have been observed -- never a hardcoded guess, always derived from this site's own real appends (design/plugins/telemetry-store/lib/store.js's stats()).

bytesPerSample.description: sizeBytes / rowCount. null until at least one row has been appended.

path.description: Absolute path to the CSV file on this site's .mdk-data root, e.g. <siteRoot>/.mdk-data/telemetry-store/telemetry.csv. Same disclosure posture as SiteReveal.storage.path/.corestore -- this is transparency about mechanics, not a secret.

sizeBytes.description: fs.statSync() of the live file at request time.

firstObservedAt.description: Unix ms of the first sample ever recorded by this plugin instance (persisted in a sidecar file so it survives a Gateway restart within the site's lifetime -- see store.js).

SiteRevealTelemetryStorage.description: New, optional sibling of SiteReveal.storage/telemetry. Present only when spec.plugins included 'telemetry-store' for this site; otherwise omitted entirely (not null) -- a site that never opted in has nothing to report here, which is a different statement from 'we tried to read it and it was unavailable' (contrast with design/site-config-v2.openrpc-fragment.json's telemetryUnavailableReason pattern for a headless-Gateway site, which IS an opt-in-shaped null).

schemas.$comment_redaction: Not a new schema, a correctness note for whoever implements this: src/server.js's revealCurl() reproduces sites.create's exact request body from record.spec. If spec.auth is ever stored with a real password or even a hash+salt inside record.spec, revealCurl()'s JSON.stringify(rpcBody) would print it right back out through sites.reveal -- exactly the leak design/plugin-basic-auth.md's password-handling section says must not happen. The concrete fix: normalize record.spec.spec.auth.password to a fixed placeholder string (e.g. '<redacted>') before it is ever stored in the SiteRecord or reproduced in requestCurl/spec.yaml -- the real salt+hash live only in the env vars passed to the child process (see design/plugin-basic-auth.md), never in the record the launcher keeps around or reveals.
